title: The rendering model: reconciliation, and what actually re-renders

videos.script:
You press a button, and a number on the screen changes. Between those two moments, React did more than you think, and less than you fear.

{{trigger}} First the planner gets something to change: buttons that move from one week to the next.

{{steps}} Then the three steps every update goes through. A trigger. A render, where React calls your components. And a commit, the only step that touches the page.

{{renders}} You will make every component announce itself on the console. Press one button, and ten components render again. All of them. Not just the ones whose props changed.

{{strict}} On the first load you will see each one twice. That is strict mode, and it is doing it on purpose.

{{dom}} Then you will count what actually changed on the page. Ten components rendered. Ten text nodes changed. Not one element was rebuilt.

{{key}} And last, where state lives. Not in a variable, not in the data. In a position in the tree. Change the key, and the state starts again.
